title: Rav Papa Saba
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman says that Rav Papa Saba always spoke in Rav’s name, as in [Kiddushin 71b](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.71b.12), [Sanhedrin 49b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.49b.5) and [Menachot 33b](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.33b.12).

Yuchasin, under Daor bar Papa, lists eleven sons of Rav Papa Saba who lived in Rav’s time. Its author writes that he heard from his father, who received the tradition from elder sages, that their names help against forgetfulness.

Sefer HaEshkol, Laws of Torah Scrolls, says that the eleven sons of Rav Papa were not all sons of one Rav Papa but lived at different times. It too preserves a tradition that their names help remove forgetfulness, and mentions the custom of reciting them at the completion of a tractate.[^1]

notes.text: [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2984&lang=en) records all three attributions and quotes Sefer Yuchasin as placing some sons in Rav’s time and others in the time of Abaye and Rava. Hyman presents the eleven-sons list alongside Sefer HaEshkol’s account.
